When PAGER is set but its command is not found, `_pipepager`/`_tempfilepager` now yield plain stdout and the caller returns immediately, so the less/more/nullpager fallback chain is skipped and output is never paged or color-stripped.

A StringIO fallback stream has `encoding` set to None, so `get_pager_file` takes the BinaryIO branch and wraps the StringIO in `MaybeStripAnsi` (a TextIOWrapper), which raises TypeError because StringIO is not a binary buffer.
The StringIO branch only sets `stream.color` and never strips ANSI, yet `should_strip_ansi` now returns False for any object with a `color` attribute, so ANSI codes leak into the non-tty output.

`should_strip_ansi` now skips stripping for any stream that has a `color` attribute, which assumes it is a MaybeStripAnsi wrapper; other streams with such an attribute will no longer have ANSI stripped.
In `_tempfilepager`, the NamedTemporaryFile is only closed on the normal path, so if the caller's body raises inside the yield the file handle leaks before the unlink in finally runs.

For a real TextIO, `MaybeStripAnsi(stream.buffer, ...)` creates a TextIOWrapper over `sys.stdout.buffer`; when that wrapper is garbage-collected it closes the underlying buffer, so later stdout writes fail with 'I/O operation on closed file'.

The comment says the stream's wrapper handles ANSI stripping so nothing should be stripped here, but `return True` tells callers to strip, so colored output is stripped whenever the stream has a `color` attribute.

A StringIO has `encoding` set to None, so it falls into the BinaryIO branch and is wrapped in TextIOWrapper, whose writes then call `.write(bytes)` on the StringIO and raise TypeError; this is the path taken when `_default_text_stdout()` returns None.

If the body of the `with` block raises, the `yield` throws, so the NamedTemporaryFile is never flushed or closed before `os.unlink`; the handle leaks and unlink fails on Windows, which the comment says this code exists to support.

When PAGER is set but its command is missing, `_pipepager` now yields plain stdout instead of returning False, so the old fallback chain to less/more/nullpager is never reached and paging is silently skipped.

When a stream has a `color` attribute, this returns True (meaning strip ANSI) regardless of that attribute's value, so output the caller asked to keep in color is stripped, and the comment's claim that MaybeStripAnsi handles stripping contradicts the return value.

A StringIO has no `buffer` and its `encoding` is None, so it falls into the `elif not getattr(stream, 'encoding')` branch and is wrapped in MaybeStripAnsi (a TextIOWrapper) instead of reaching the intended `stream.color = color` branch, which raises when the pager is a StringIO.

MaybeStripAnsi wraps the existing `stream.buffer` of sys.stdout, and when the wrapper is garbage-collected TextIOWrapper closes that shared buffer, so subsequent writes to the real stdout fail with 'I/O operation on closed file'.

The fallback chain was removed: if PAGER names a missing command or `less` is absent, the code now returns a no-op stdout instead of trying `more`/a temp file or the null pager, so paged output is silently written without paging and the prior fallbacks are lost.

The `color` detection from LESS flags runs before `color` is defaulted, and the subsequent `if color is None: color = False` is placed after it, so behavior for the `less` case where the user passed `color=None` depends on ordering that no longer matches the original decision logic.

The OSError handling around `subprocess.call` was removed and the temp file is not closed if the body raises, so a missing or unlaunchable pager command now raises OSError to the caller and the file can leak on Windows where unlink then fails.
